_comment: Copy to config.local.json and fill in. Anything set here overrides the same upper-case name in config.py. Unknown keys are reported and ignored.
_comment2: This file is gitignored. Nothing personal should ever be in config.py.
USER_NAME: your name, spoken in the system prompt and confirmations
CITY: your city, for the briefing's weather line
_comment3: Your own words for the recogniser, added to the project's own list in config.py. Your name, your town, the programs you launch by voice: without these, whisper guesses at proper nouns and the app you open every day comes back wrong.
_comment4: The phrase that wakes it, and the variants the recogniser may produce for its last word. The phrase is understood, not matched against a trained model, so any phrase works. The aliases matter when the name is unusual: whisper will not spell it the same way twice.
WHISPER_HINT_EXTRA: your name, your town, the apps you launch by voice
_comment5: Answering with no internet. Needs a local model: install llama.cpp and a Vulkan or CUDA backend for it, put a GGUF in PI_LOCAL_MODELS_DIR, and point pi at it by adding a provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json whose baseUrl is the router (http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1). Leave the list empty and none of this exists.
_comment6: auto follows the network, online never goes local, offline never calls a relay and is how the local path gets tested without unplugging anything.
_comment7: ARCHY starts the router itself when the offline chain needs it, and stops only one it started.
_comment8: Off by default, and off means no gate and no enforcement. On means every tool call is judged in code before it runs: reading and writing inside its own directories, and commands that only look, are allowed; anything else waits for your approval, once, for that exact action. A policy that cannot be read denies everything. Ask what is waiting with 'python -m archy.permissions list', allow one with 'approve', or by voice.
_comment9: Extra directories the assistant may touch without asking. Its own directory and .state are always included. The home directory is not: approving everything a program can reach is the same as having no gate.
_comment10: What may leave the machine when an online model is answering. All of these default to on, which is what the assistant already did: a privacy setting that changes behaviour on upgrade is not a setting. With the local model answering, none of it leaves the machine anyway, so these only affect relays. Enforced in code where the request is built, never by asking the model to keep quiet. Ask what is switched off by voice, or with `python -m archy.privacy status`.
_comment11: The dashboard's second panel: which model is answering, the network, what may leave the machine, what waits on approval. Off by default.
